fatal_errors: The proposed polycrystalline compression-versus-tension study does not reconstruct the target single-crystal tensile molecular-dynamics investigation along specified crystallographic orientations.
The clustering-to-ordering mechanism conflicts with the target mechanism of vacancy-assisted Shockley-partial nucleation and stacking-fault-mediated plasticity.
The sole evidence concerns Al0.1CrCoFeNi, containing both Al and Co, rather than equiatomic Co-free FeNiCrMn; its ordering correlations are therefore not transferable without direct support.

The predicted loading-mode-dependent strain hardening omits the target outcomes: orientation anisotropy, temperature softening, strain-rate-insensitive yield strength, increased dislocation density at high rates, and absence of BCC transformation or twinning.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses mechanical behavior of an HEA and proposes a reasonably falsifiable compression–tension comparison, but it is scientifically disconnected from the hidden target. It changes the material state from an FCC single crystal to a conventionally produced polycrystal, substitutes compression-induced chemical ordering for tensile dislocation physics, and does not specify the target orientations or MD strain-rate range. Some temperatures broadly overlap, but the conditions and reference baseline do not reproduce the target design. The experiment could discriminate its own alternative hypothesis, although conventional diffraction may have limited sensitivity to short-range order. Most importantly, E1 studies a chemically different Al- and Co-containing alloy under MD conditions, so it cannot validly support a clustering-to-ordering transition in equiatomic FeNiCrMn.
